one_liner: Drop-in ELF linker beating LLVM lld and GNU ld via pervasive data-parallelism across the whole link pipeline.
what_it_does: mold is a from-scratch Unix/Linux ELF linker invoked as a drop-in replacement for GNU ld/gold/lld via the compiler's `-fuse-ld=mold` flag (or `-B` for GCC before 12.1) — same CLI surface, no API to learn. It links user-land executables and shared libraries on 16 ELF architecture variants (x86-64, i386, ARM32/64, RISC-V32/64, PowerPC32/64, s390x, LoongArch32/64, SPARC64, m68k, SH-4) and implements only a minimal linker-script subset, just enough to parse glibc's ASCII `libc.so` loader script. Written by LLVM lld's original author; in production use since 2021 and the default linker for many large open-source projects.
how_it_is_fast: Per the ASPLOS 2027 paper ('mold: A Massively Parallel Linker'), mold decouples the traditionally entangled passes of Unix linking — symbol resolution, archive-member pulling, relocation, output layout — so each stage is split across a rayon-based work-stealing thread pool (capped at 32 threads by default) instead of running mostly single-threaded like lld/gold. Section-merging deduplication uses a custom lock-free, open-addressing concurrent hash map (CAS-claimed buckets, per-shard probing) whose table size is pre-estimated with HyperLogLog cardinality counting rather than grown/resized on the fly. The paper's ablation study found no single optimization dominates — the speedup is cumulative across nearly every pass being parallelized.
when_to_use: Large C/C++/Rust ELF builds on Linux/Unix where the link step dominates the debug-edit-rebuild loop — mold shows 4x-16x over lld on multi-GB debug binaries (per-program table in README).
Many-core workstations or CI runners (Threadripper-class) where lld/gold leave most cores idle during linking.
Toolchains that already select a linker via `-fuse-ld=`/`-B` (Clang, GCC 12.1+, Rust via `.cargo/config.toml`) — swapping in mold is a one-line config change.
Any of the 16 listed non-Windows/non-macOS ELF targets, including cross-linking ARM64 output from an x86 host.
Teams that want bit-for-bit deterministic link output with no host-specific default paths baked in.
when_not_to_use: Native Windows/MSVC or macOS/Mach-O link jobs: the mold.exe binary builds and runs on Windows, but per the maintainer (issue #1658) it 'can only be used to link ELF binaries' — no PE/COFF or Mach-O support, and macOS support was explicitly ruled out (issue #1052 thread).

Projects relying on non-trivial linker-script features (custom SECTIONS/memory layouts, embedded/microcontroller link maps) — mold supports only the minimal subset needed to parse glibc's loader script and has stated no plan to add more (open issue #243, 'SECTIONS doesn't seem to be implemented').
Workloads needing incremental or partial linking (gold-style `--incremental`, or `-r` combined with LTO) — not supported; every invocation is a full relink.
Small link jobs on few-core machines: on the M1 Ultra debug table mold actually regressed vs. lld for Clang (0.9x) — the parallel design needs enough cores/input size to pay for itself.

If you need long field-history on the exact codebase in production: the linker rewrote from C++ to Rust just before this snapshot (Sept 2026, issue #1655), so 'production since 2021' applies to the predecessor C++ implementation, not the current Rust one.

integration.form: crate (Cargo workspace building a CLI binary `mold` + companion shared object `mold-wrapper.so`; not a library you link against)
integration.dependencies: Rust crates: rayon, hashbrown, memmap2, blake3, xxhash-rust, crc32fast, zstd, flate2, libz-sys, cpp_demangle, rustc-demangle, bstr, memchr, getrandom, libc. Build also needs a C compiler (GCC/Clang) and Git.
integration.min_toolchain: Rust stable toolchain (Cargo.toml workspace edition 2024, i.e. rustc 1.85+); rust-toolchain.toml pins channel "stable".
integration.platforms: Linux/Unix ELF targets: x86-64, i386, ARM32/64 (+BE), RISC-V32/64 (+BE), PowerPC32/64 (v1/v2), s390x, LoongArch32/64, SPARC64, m68k, SH-4. Also builds on Windows (CI job build-windows.ps1 produces mold.exe) but, per the maintainer, can then only link ELF output, not PE/COFF.
integration.thread_safety: Not documented as a library API (mold is CLI-only, no embeddable interface). Internally rayon-driven; thread count defaults to min(cores,32) and is configurable via --thread-count/--no-threads. Output is documented as deterministic/bit-for-bit reproducible regardless of thread scheduling.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — CLI-compatible drop-in via -fuse-ld=mold/-B (same invocation mechanism and most flags as GNU ld/lld for ordinary builds), but only a minimal linker-script subset is implemented, so builds relying on custom scripts (SECTIONS etc.) will not work.

gotchas: --start-group/--end-group are accepted for compatibility but silently ignored — mold (like lld) tracks archive symbols globally so link order doesn't matter, which can surprise anyone relying on that flag's traditional semantics.
No incremental or partial (-r + LTO) linking; every run is a full relink.
Only a minimal linker-script subset is supported (just enough to read glibc's ASCII libc.so loader script); no plans to extend it.
Windows builds of the CLI exist but only link ELF, not PE/COFF — don't expect an MSVC linker replacement.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick mold over wild when you need broader architecture coverage (16 ISAs vs. wild's more limited set) or maximum throughput on many-core Linux boxes: mold is ~1.9x faster than wild at the median, and wild is marked N/A (can't link at all) on several rows in mold's own table, including Chromium release builds because it lacks --icf=all. mold and zld don't really compete — zld targets Apple's ld64/Mach-O toolchain exclusively, so on macOS zld is the only option of the two; mold has explicitly ruled out macOS support.
verified_claims_summary: On 9 real-world programs (Blender, Chromium, Clang, ClickHouse, Firefox, Godot, LibreOffice, PyTorch, TensorFlow, some ARM64 variants) linked in both debug and release configurations, mold beat LLVM lld by 4.9x at the median (per-program range ~1.5x-16.1x) and wild by 1.9x at the median. All three linkers were built from source in release mode as of 2026-08-28 with default options; measurements are wall-clock, median of 3 runs after a warm-up, on an AMD Ryzen Threadripper 7980X/Ubuntu 24.04 and an Apple M1 Ultra/Fedora Asahi Remix 42.
status_note: Actively maintained (last commit 2026-09-23; 140+ contributors; CI test-builds ~19,000 Gentoo packages against GNU ld as a control before each release); MIT-licensed with prebuilt binaries via most distro package managers and GitHub releases, though the linker core is a very recent (Sept 2026) full rewrite from C++ to Rust.
